correctness.rationale: Direct reconstruction gives the anchored Gram G=((2-q)J+qI+(q-1)A)/2 with q=2^p; the 2-regular component structure diagonalizes it into global, intercomponent and local Fourier sectors. Every critical eigenvalue is an affine function of q and the earliest zero gives the exact interval. For odd maximum rim L, a tie would make 2cos(pi/L) a nonintegral rational algebraic integer, impossible. Gram rank gives endpoint Hilbert affine dimension; all quantifiers are over finite disjoint-cycle cones and real zero-sum loads. The packaged checker independently forms distance Gram matrices and replayed 499 Jacobi-eigenvalue comparisons. Numerical tests are not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Cones over cycle unions are a natural extension of the wheel family to multiple interacting rim components. The theorem determines not only a sharp infinite-family embedding threshold but the structural switch from rim-local to globally supported extremal signed measures, forbids resonance arithmetically, and exhibits arbitrarily large critical embedding-dimension drops. Shorter cycles act only through total size until the global phase. Those effects are not supplied as a closed classification by general determinant criteria, and are relevant to sharp snowflake Hilbert dimension and negative-type obstructions.
